newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovnaft pushes Slovak bourse slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Slovnaft pushes Slovak bourse slightly higher.

text.p: Major Slovak stocks closed mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, but gains to the average price of shares of oil refiner Slovnaft pushed the SAX index up 0.43 points to 206.38.
Slovnaft closed down nine crowns at its nominal value of 1,000, but its average price -- used for calculating the index -- rose 2.3 percent.
"Larger Slovnaft packages are available for about 1,025 crowns, as this was also the case of today's trade," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
He added that the BSE appears unaffected by the current downtrend on the neighbouring markets, and predicted the bourse to hold at current levels, or post a slight increase, in the mid-term.
"Even after including the potential risk of the political situation, our market is still undervalued compared with other bourses in the region," he said.

Brokers said the SAX could again push above 207 points, its 1997 yeay high, as foreign demand for the most attractive issues, such as Slovnaft, steel maker VSZ, drug producer Slovakofarma or builder Vahostav continues.
VSZ closed down five crowns at 695, while Slovakofarma rose 17 crowns to 4,900 and Vahostav fell 20 crowns to 2,400.
Overall volume rose to 374,909 shares, boosted by direct trades, from 218,240 stocks traded on Wednesday. Turnover increased to 211.58 million crowns, from 178.6 million.
